correctness.rationale: Independently substituting rho=(K-1)/(K+n-2) in the equicorrelation inverse gives D=dI and kappa_star=(1+(n-2)rho)/(1-rho)=K; ordinary kappa=(1+(n-1)rho)/(1-rho)=K+(K-1)/(n-1). Gaussian arcsine law yields largest sign covariance eigenvalue 1+2(n-1)arcsin(rho)/pi. For a=K-1, t=n-1, derivative of t arcsin(a/(a+t)) is arcsin(r)-r sqrt((1-r)/(1+r))>0 for r in (0,1); the limit is a. MGF variance proxy must dominate covariance. Roth’s Gaussian-sign upper bound supplies the advertised K proxy. No equality for the optimal MGF proxy or global extremality is claimed.

value.rationale: The limiting example identifies a natural sharpness boundary for a recently strengthened Gaussian sign concentration constant: each pair correlation vanishes while a normalized sum still has variance asymptotic to 1+2(K-1)/pi. It distinguishes global dependence from pairwise correlation, not merely rewriting a theorem parameter.

limitations: Sharpness over the positive equicorrelation slice only, not all covariances.
The limit n→infinity occurs at fixed K>1 and only afterward K→infinity for ratio pi/2.
